narrative.summary: Seychelles has no AI law, and no national AI strategy has been published. Its AI governance rests on the Data Protection Act 2023, which covers profiling, requires impact assessments for automated decision-making and gives the Information Commission a review role, and on the National Artificial Intelligence in Education Framework 2026-2030 of the Ministry of Education, which sets rules for AI use in schools, including approved and prohibited AI tools. The National Institute of Science, Technology and Innovation Act 2025, in force since 13 April 2026, tasks the new Institute with devising strategies to promote the use of AI. A private member's AI bill has been discussed but not tabled.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Education and Human Resource Development
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026 from the official gazette and ministry websites. Not yet verified from the official text: material from the telecoms regulator, the procurement board and the National Assembly's bills pages. The proposed AI bill and the AI code of practice for schools are tracked as leads. A national digital and AI strategy for 2026-2031, approved by the Council of Ministers according to press coverage, is tracked as a lead until its official text is published.

instruments.issuing_authority: National Assembly of Seychelles; assented by the President of the Republic
instruments.current_status: Passed by the National Assembly on 5 December 2023, assented 19 December 2023 and published as a supplement to the Official Gazette of 22 December 2023, repealing the Data Protection Act (Cap 57); the Act has no separate commencement section, and the Information Commission states it came into effect following its passage in December 2023. Section 56 gave existing controllers and processors 18 months from commencement to comply, and no regulations under s.30(2) on solely automated significant decisions have been found in the Gazette.
instruments.summary: Seychelles' general data protection law, applying to public and private processing of personal data by automatic, semi-automatic and manual means and enforced by the Information Commission. It defines 'profiling', requires a data protection impact assessment before systematic and extensive automated evaluation (including profiling) on which decisions with legal or similarly significant effects are based, tasks the Commission with examining any proposal for automated decision-making that may affect privacy, and lets the Minister make regulations safeguarding data subjects against significant decisions based solely on automated processing.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: The only Seychelles statute with explicit automated decision-making and profiling provisions; governs personal data used to train and run AI systems.
instruments.publisher_name: National Assembly of Seychelles; assented by the President of the Republic
instruments.scope: Processing of personal data in Seychelles by public and private bodies (excluding criminal investigation, national security and purely personal activity)

instruments.official_title: National Artificial Intelligence in Education Framework, Seychelles 2026–2030
instruments.english_title: National Artificial Intelligence in Education Framework, Seychelles 2026–2030
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Education and Human Resource Development
instruments.current_status: Cover dated March 2026; posted in the Ministry's Frameworks download section (listed 29 July 2026). The document states it has been endorsed by the World Bank; no adoption date is recorded. Not yet verified from the official text: Cabinet approval. It provides for a National AI in Education Steering Committee, an AI Code of Practice for Schools and approved/prohibited AI tools lists, none of which were found published yet.
instruments.summary: Five-year framework (2026–2030) from the Ministry of Education and Human Resource Development for introducing AI in Seychelles state schools in a safe, ethical and human-centred way. It establishes a National AI in Education Steering Committee to set direction and approve AI tools against safety, data protection and pedagogical criteria, requires a nationally maintained Approved Educational AI Tools List and Prohibited Tools List to guide procurement and classroom use, and requires each school to designate an AI Lead Teacher. It sets ethical and legal safeguards (data protection, child safeguarding, transparency, bias mitigation, academic integrity) and bars high-stakes uses such as fully automated final grading, certification or student placement decisions, alongside teacher competency, curriculum, KPI and roadmap sections.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Seychelles' first government AI policy document; the de facto public-sector AI governance framework for the education system.
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Education and Human Resource Development
instruments.scope: State schools in Seychelles (primary and secondary), education leadership and school administration
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): Ministry download page (edu.gov.sc Frameworks section, listed 29 July 2026) and full 21-page PDF read (pdftotext); cover dated March 2026

instruments.official_title: National Institute of Science, Technology and Innovation Act, 2025 (Act 24 of 2025)
instruments.english_title: National Institute of Science, Technology and Innovation Act, 2025 (Act 24 of 2025)
instruments.issuing_authority: National Assembly of Seychelles; assented by the President of the Republic
instruments.current_status: Assented 22 December 2025 and published in the Supplement to the Official Gazette of 23 December 2025; brought into operation on 13 April 2026 by the National Institute of Science, Technology and Innovation (Commencement) Notice 2026 (S.I. 25 of 2026, made 9 April 2026, Gazette supplement of 10 April 2026).
instruments.summary: Establishes the National Institute of Science, Technology and Innovation as a body corporate to coordinate national science, technology and innovation (STI) research, funding, technology transfer and innovation infrastructure. Among its eight statutory objectives, section 4(1)(h) tasks it to devise strategies, collaborate and 'promote the use of Artificial Intelligence, other emerging technologies and digitisation' as tools for socio-economic development, and section 10(2)(b) allows its funds to finance STI projects 'including the use of Artificial Intelligence'.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Gives a national statutory body a mandate to devise strategies promoting AI use and to fund AI projects.
instruments.publisher_name: National Assembly of Seychelles; assented by the President of the Republic

Bill No. 27 of 2025 (dated 5 December 2025) also read. Published in: Official Gazette of the Republic of Seychelles.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Seychelles' official gazette, the ICT department, ministries and regulators were searched.
